correctness.rationale: Exact state conservation gives R_n=2K_n. The weak-edge hazard is at most w_n/4, yielding uniform exponential moments. A stopped quadratic supermartingale bounds imbalance by O_P(sqrt n); consequently the conditional rare-edge hazard is uniformly lambda/(4n)+o_P(1/n) while at least epsilon n small-class vertices remain. Coupling to iid Bernoulli rare events and bounding the terminal epsilon n step layer establishes Poisson(lambda/2) and all moments. Independent labelled-vertex and lumped rational recursions, analytic inequalities and seeded simulations checked in included verify.py, 52 tests.

value.rationale: The class capacities (n,n,2n) impose a natural exact conservation rule; every rare direct small-class reaction leaves exactly two final defects. The inverse-system-size rate is the nontrivial crossover between complete exhaustion and a random finite defect population, determining all limiting probabilities and moments. It resolves a motivated microscopic boundary invisible in fixed-weight macroscopic density limits.
